spec.description: Sends a batch of 2-15 orders in a single request, all sharing one pair. Validation runs against the whole batch before submission to the engine -- if any order fails validation, the whole batch is rejected. Once submitted, an order failing a pre-match check (e.g. insufficient funding) is rejected individually and the rest of the batch is processed.

request.title: BatchAddParams
request.description: Parameters for submitting a batch of 2-15 orders in a single request, all on one pair. Validation runs against the whole batch before submission -- one invalid order rejects the entire batch. On submission, an individual order failing a pre-match check (e.g. insufficient funding) is rejected on its own and the rest of the batch is processed.

deadline.description: RFC3339 timestamp, millisecond precision. Valid offsets from the current time range from 500ms to 60s (default 5s). The engine will not match orders in this batch after this time.

symbol.description: The symbol of the currency pair for every order in the batch, e.g. `BTC/USD`.

validate.description: If `true`, every order in the batch is validated only -- none reaches the matching engine.

orders.title: BatchOrderList
orders.description: The orders in the batch, 2 to 15 of them, all on `symbol`.

anyOf.title: WsBatchOrderMarket
anyOf.description: A market order within a batch_add request: executes immediately at the best available price.

order_type.description: The execution model of the order.

order_qty.description: Order quantity in terms of the base asset.

effective_time.description: Scheduled start time, RFC3339, precision to seconds.

expire_time.description: Expiration time of the order, RFC3339, precision to seconds. GTD orders only; can expire up to one month in the future.

fee_preference.description: Fee preference, base or quote currency. `quote` is the default for buy orders, `base` is the default for sell orders.

margin.description: Funds the order on margin using the maximum leverage for the pair (max leverage of 5).

no_mpp.description: Deprecated -- if supplied, accepted but ignored. Was: disable Market Price Protection for market orders.

cl_ord_id.description: Alphanumeric client order identifier uniquely identifying this order. Mutually exclusive with `order_userref`. One of: a long UUID (32 hex chars, dashed), a short UUID (32 hex chars, no dashes), or free text up to 18 ASCII characters.

order_userref.description: Optional non-unique numeric identifier associable with any number of orders by the client. Mutually exclusive with `cl_ord_id`.

post_only.description: Cancels the order if it would take liquidity on arrival. For orders with a limit price only.

reduce_only.description: Reduces an existing margin position without opening an opposite position worth more than the current value of the leveraged assets.

stp_type.description: Self Trade Prevention mode: `cancel_newest` (cancel the arriving order), `cancel_oldest` (cancel the resting order), or `cancel_both`.

time_in_force.description: How long the order remains in effect before expiring: `gtc`, `gtd` (until `expire_time`), `ioc` (cancels any unfilled remainder on arrival), or `fok` (fills fully or cancels entirely; `limit` orders only).

sender_sub_id.description: Alphanumeric sub-account/trader identifier enabling Self Trade Prevention at a more granular level, for institutional accounts with enhanced STP.

trigger.description: Deprecated -- use `triggers.reference`. Triggered order types only.

cash_order_qty.description: Order volume expressed in the quote currency. Market orders only.

notes: `token` (the auth bearer token) is documented by Kraken as a required params field but is deliberately absent from this schema: `core/transport/ws.py`'s `SocketConnection.rpc_send` merges the cached token into every outgoing `params` on the private connection -- trading calls and subscribe/unsubscribe alike -- so it is transport-injected, never a caller-supplied argument, the same way `req_id` (the declared `correlate` field) never appears in a requestBody schema. `orders` is a variable-length list of same-shaped order specs, so it is modeled as a plain array with `items` pointing at the titled `BatchOrderSpec` schema (shared, structurally, with `add_order`'s top-level fields minus `symbol`/`token` which are batch-level) rather than `prefixItems`, which is for fixed-shape tuples. `result` is itself an array (one entry per submitted order) rather than a single object, unlike every other command in this batch of eight.
